full_judgment:
13. The cardinal principles of the criminal jurisprudence is the presumption of innocence of the accused and the burden of proving the guilt of the accused is on the prosecution which must prove the charge substantially as laid ie, to prove to the hilt and beyond all reasonable doubt. There fundamental principles have been incorporated both in substantive and procedural law. This principle is based on the legal maxim that, 10 accused persons be acquitted of the charge but not a single innocent person be punished. 

 16. Evidence adduced from the prosecution side had been detailed above. On analysis of the evidences of prosecution witnesses it appears that except Informant PW 1 there is no eye-witness as to the hijacking of Taka 20,000.00 by accused-appellants. No other PWs testified that they were present at the time of the alleged commission of offence of hijacking by the accused-appellants. It is true that under section 134 of the Evidence Act conviction can be awarded on the basis of a solitary testimony of a single witness if the same is an unimpeached piece of evidence and is at all believable. But it is also equally true that conviction on the basis of the testimony of a solitary witness is not at all safe and corroboration is a must. In the case in our hand we do not find any corroboration supporting the testimony of the PW 1 as to the alleged snatching away of Taka 20,000.00 from him. It appears from the testimony of PW 7, the Investigating Officer that the neighbouring persons of the place of occurrence were not examined in support of the prosecution case. This non-examination of the neighbouring witnesses raises a presumption that had all the neighbouring witnesses been examined they would not have supported the prosecution case.
